sections.content: Some verbs end in *-ik* in the dictionary: *dolgozik* (works), *reggelizik* (has breakfast), *eszik* (eats), *iszik* (drinks). For he and she the *-ik* stays: *Anna dolgozik.* For “I” these verbs take *-om / -em / -öm* instead of *-ok / -ek / -ök*: *dolgozom, reggelizem, eszem, iszom*. In every other person they use the endings you know, on the stem: *dolgozol, dolgozunk, dolgoztok, dolgoznak*.

Regular verbs keep their usual “I” ending: *főzök, olvasok*. Only “I” and he or she are different in an *-ik* verb. You already know this pattern from *lakom*. What you eat or drink goes before the verb and takes *-t* (unit 19): *teát iszom*.

items.english: In the morning I drink coffee.

sections.content: *Dolgozok* is the usual mistake. A verb that ends in *-ik* in the dictionary says “I” with *-om / -em / -öm*: *dolgozom*, *iszom*, never *iszok*. And keep the *-ik* for he and she: *Anna dolgozik*, not *Anna dolgoz*.
